topic: How do GEO vs LEO satellite orbits affect latency and coverage in hybrid networks for rural substation monitoring?
consensus_response: GEO offers high capacity but suffers from significant delay due to propagation, while LEO satellites provide lower latency but face reliability challenges. Hybrid networks leveraging both orbits can optimize this tradeoff. Adaptive routing protocols dynamically adjust data paths based on signal quality and latency constraints for optimal performance in dynamic environments.
reference_context: Satellite communications systems offer global wireless coverage with enhanced data rates, enabling seamless connectivity between terrestrial networks. LEO satellites, deployed at low altitudes (500-2000 km), provide faster communication speeds and reduced delays compared to GEO counterparts.  This makes them suitable for applications like 5G mmTC and EMMB, as well as ultra-reliable communications (URC) with high availability and reliability.
